blocks.en: What Amillennialism Holds
blocks.es_reference: Lo que Sostiene el Amilenialismo

blocks.en: This unit presents the third of the three main views of the millennium, amillennialism, and the course continues to hold the three views side by side, presenting each at full strength and favoring none. The prefix "a" means "no," and so the name signals that this view expects no literal, earthly thousand-year reign of Christ following His return. Instead, amillennialism teaches that the thousand years of Revelation 20 are a symbol of the entire present age, the whole span between the first and second comings of Christ. During this age Christ reigns now from heaven over His kingdom, the souls of the faithful who have died live and reign with Him, and Satan is restrained from deceiving the nations so as to stop the spread of the gospel. There is, in this view, no separate earthly kingdom between Christ's return and the eternal state. When Christ comes again, there is one general resurrection of the righteous and the wicked, one final judgment, and then immediately the new heaven and the new earth. Amillennialism therefore reads Revelation 20 as describing the church age in which believers now live, rather than a future period on earth, and it understands the millennium as a present spiritual reality rather than a coming political one. Amillennialists also emphasize how the book first spoke to its original readers. Revelation was written to a church under heavy persecution, and its first purpose was not to chart events thousands of years away but to assure suffering believers that their tribulation was bounded, that the beast and the mark of chapter thirteen wore a first-century face in the Roman emperor cult, and that Christ already reigns and will surely triumph. Read in this way, the thousand years of the present age are the very age in which the persecuted church lives and reigns with her enthroned Lord, and the book is heard as a word of comfort and endurance rather than a calendar of the distant future.
blocks.es_reference: Esta unidad presenta la tercera de las tres vistas principales del milenio, el amilenialismo, y el curso sigue sosteniendo las tres vistas lado a lado, presentando cada una a plena fuerza y sin favorecer a ninguna. El prefijo "a" significa "no," y así el nombre señala que esta vista no espera ningún reinado terrenal literal de mil años de Cristo después de su regreso. En cambio, el amilenialismo enseña que los mil años de Apocalipsis 20 son un símbolo de toda la presente edad, el lapso entero entre la primera y la segunda venida de Cristo. Durante esta edad Cristo reina ahora desde el cielo sobre su reino, las almas de los fieles que han muerto viven y reinan con él, y Satanás es contenido de engañar a las naciones de modo que detenga la difusión del evangelio. No hay, en esta vista, un reino terrenal separado entre el regreso de Cristo y el estado eterno. Cuando Cristo venga otra vez, hay una resurrección general de los justos y los impíos, un juicio final, y entonces inmediatamente el nuevo cielo y la nueva tierra. El amilenialismo por tanto lee Apocalipsis 20 como describiendo la edad de la iglesia en que los creyentes ahora viven, más que un período futuro en la tierra, y entiende el milenio como una realidad espiritual presente más que una venidera y política. Los amilenialistas también destacan cómo el libro habló primero a sus lectores originales. El Apocalipsis fue escrito a una iglesia bajo fuerte persecución, y su primer propósito no era trazar eventos a miles de años de distancia sino asegurar a los creyentes que sufrían que su tribulación era limitada, que la bestia y la marca del capítulo trece llevaban un rostro del primer siglo en el culto al emperador romano, y que Cristo ya reina y ciertamente triunfará. Leído de esta manera, los mil años de la presente edad son la misma edad en que la iglesia perseguida vive y reina con su Señor entronizado, y el libro se oye como una palabra de consuelo y perseverancia más que un calendario del futuro distante.

blocks.en: The Order of Events
blocks.es_reference: El Orden de los Acontecimientos

blocks.en: The amillennial order is the simplest of the three. The present church age is itself the millennium, the time in which Christ reigns from heaven, the gospel goes to the nations, and the departed saints reign with Christ. Throughout this age, amillennialists hold, the kingdom grows and the gospel spreads, but evil also continues and even intensifies, for the wheat and the tares grow together until the harvest, and both ripen toward the end. There is no earthly golden age to be expected before the return, as in one of the other views, nor an earthly reign to follow it, as in the other. At the close of the age Satan is loosed for a little while in a final assault, which is the brief loosing of Revelation 20. Then Christ returns, once and visibly. At His single coming the dead are raised, the righteous and the wicked together, in one general resurrection; all stand before the great white throne for one final judgment; and then God brings in the new heaven and the new earth at once. So the whole drama turns on one return, one resurrection, and one judgment, without any thousand-year reign on the earth before or after.
blocks.es_reference: El orden amilenial es el más sencillo de los tres. La presente edad de la iglesia es ella misma el milenio, el tiempo en que Cristo reina desde el cielo, el evangelio va a las naciones, y los santos que han partido reinan con Cristo. A lo largo de esta edad, sostienen los amilenialistas, el reino crece y el evangelio se difunde, pero el mal también continúa y aun se intensifica, pues el trigo y la cizaña crecen juntos hasta la siega, y ambos maduran hacia el fin. No hay una edad de oro terrenal que esperar antes del regreso, como en una de las otras vistas, ni un reinado terrenal que le siga, como en la otra. Al cierre de la edad Satanás es suelto por un poco de tiempo en un asalto final, que es el breve soltar de Apocalipsis 20. Entonces Cristo regresa, una vez y visiblemente. En su única venida los muertos son resucitados, los justos y los impíos juntos, en una resurrección general; todos están delante del gran trono blanco para un juicio final; y entonces Dios trae el nuevo cielo y la nueva tierra de una vez. Así todo el drama gira sobre un regreso, una resurrección, y un juicio, sin ningún reinado de mil años en la tierra antes o después.

blocks.en: The Biblical Case for Amillennialism
blocks.es_reference: El Caso Bíblico del Amilenialismo

blocks.en: Amillennialists build their case from the wider New Testament as well as from Revelation. They argue that the "first resurrection" of Revelation 20 is a spiritual rather than a bodily rising. Some take it as the new birth, since Scripture speaks of believers as already raised with Christ and made alive together with Him while they live on earth (John 5:24-25; Ephesians 2:1-6); others take it as the entrance of the believer's soul into life and reign with Christ at death. They appeal for the binding of Satan to the victory of Christ's first coming, when the strong man was bound, Satan fell like lightning, and the ruler of this world was cast out (Matthew 12:29; Luke 10:18; John 12:31), so that the nations he once held in darkness now hear the gospel. They stress that the rest of the New Testament presents the second coming as a single event that brings the resurrection of all, the final judgment, and the new creation together, not in stages separated by a thousand years (John 5:28-29; 2 Peter 3:10-13). And they point to the many texts that show Christ already enthroned and reigning now, until He has put all His enemies under His feet (Acts 2:32-36; 1 Corinthians 15:25; Ephesians 1:20-22).
blocks.es_reference: Los amilenialistas edifican su caso a partir del Nuevo Testamento más amplio así como de Apocalipsis. Argumentan que la "primera resurrección" de Apocalipsis 20 es un levantarse espiritual más que corporal. Algunos la toman como el nuevo nacimiento, pues la Escritura habla de los creyentes como ya resucitados con Cristo y vivificados juntamente con él mientras viven en la tierra (Juan 5:24-25; Efesios 2:1-6); otros la toman como la entrada del alma del creyente a la vida y al reinado con Cristo en la muerte. Apelan para el atar de Satanás a la victoria de la primera venida de Cristo, cuando el hombre fuerte fue atado, Satanás cayó como un rayo, y el príncipe de este mundo fue echado fuera (Mateo 12:29; Lucas 10:18; Juan 12:31), de modo que las naciones que él una vez retuvo en tinieblas ahora oyen el evangelio. Destacan que el resto del Nuevo Testamento presenta la segunda venida como un solo evento que trae la resurrección de todos, el juicio final, y la nueva creación juntos, no en etapas separadas por mil años (Juan 5:28-29; 2 Pedro 3:10-13). Y señalan los muchos textos que muestran a Cristo ya entronizado y reinando ahora, hasta que haya puesto a todos sus enemigos debajo de sus pies (Hechos 2:32-36; 1 Corintios 15:25; Efesios 1:20-22).

blocks.en: How Amillennialism Reads Revelation 20
blocks.es_reference: Cómo Lee el Amilenialismo Apocalipsis 20

blocks.en: The key to the amillennial reading is that Revelation often circles back over the same ground, showing the same period again and again from new angles, as it does with the seals, the trumpets, and the bowls. On this principle, called recapitulation, chapter twenty does not follow chapter nineteen in time but returns to the beginning of the present age and views it afresh. The thousand years are taken as a symbolic number, signifying a long and complete period rather than a literal span of exactly one thousand calendar years. The binding of Satan is his restraint, by the power of Christ's first coming, from deceiving the nations so as to prevent the gospel from going out to them; he is bound for that purpose, though still active in other ways. The first resurrection is the spiritual life and reign of believers, whether in regeneration or in the life of the soul with Christ after death. At the end of the age Satan is loosed briefly, and then come the return of Christ and the one judgment of the closing verses of the chapter. So Revelation 20, read this way, pictures the present age and not a future earthly kingdom.
blocks.es_reference: La clave de la lectura amilenial es que Apocalipsis a menudo regresa sobre el mismo terreno, mostrando el mismo período una y otra vez desde nuevos ángulos, como lo hace con los sellos, las trompetas, y las copas. Sobre este principio, llamado recapitulación, el capítulo veinte no sigue al capítulo diecinueve en el tiempo sino que regresa al comienzo de la presente edad y la ve de nuevo. Los mil años se toman como un número simbólico, que significa un período largo y completo más que un lapso literal de exactamente mil años de calendario. El atar de Satanás es su contención, por el poder de la primera venida de Cristo, de engañar a las naciones de modo que impida que el evangelio salga a ellas; es atado para ese propósito, aunque sigue activo de otras maneras. La primera resurrección es la vida espiritual y el reinado de los creyentes, sea en la regeneración o en la vida del alma con Cristo después de la muerte. Al fin de la edad Satanás es suelto brevemente, y entonces vienen el regreso de Cristo y el único juicio de los versículos finales del capítulo. Así Apocalipsis 20, leído de esta manera, retrata la presente edad y no un reino terrenal futuro.

blocks.en: Proponents and History
blocks.es_reference: Proponentes e Historia

blocks.en: Amillennialism has the longest record as the majority view of the church through most of its history. The decisive figure was Augustine, whose work The City of God set out the reading that the thousand years are the present age and that the reign of the saints is spiritual. Under his influence the church largely turned away from the earlier expectation of an earthly reign, and amillennialism became the dominant view of the medieval church for a thousand years. The Reformers, including Luther and Calvin, stood broadly in this tradition, though the technical terms came later. The view remains common in Roman Catholic, Lutheran, and much of Reformed theology to this day. In modern times it has been carefully expounded by scholars such as Geerhardus Vos, Louis Berkhof, Anthony Hoekema, and William Hendriksen, the last of whom set out the recapitulation reading of Revelation in detail. So amillennialism is not a recent novelty but the ancient and widely held reading of the church, defended by many of its most respected teachers across the centuries.
blocks.es_reference: El amilenialismo tiene el registro más largo como la vista mayoritaria de la iglesia durante la mayor parte de su historia. La figura decisiva fue Agustín, cuya obra La Ciudad de Dios expuso la lectura de que los mil años son la presente edad y de que el reinado de los santos es espiritual. Bajo su influencia la iglesia en gran parte se apartó de la anterior expectativa de un reinado terrenal, y el amilenialismo llegó a ser la vista dominante de la iglesia medieval por mil años. Los Reformadores, incluidos Lutero y Calvino, estuvieron ampliamente en esta tradición, aunque los términos técnicos vinieron después. La vista sigue siendo común en la teología católica romana, luterana, y gran parte de la reformada hasta el día de hoy. En tiempos modernos ha sido cuidadosamente expuesta por eruditos como Geerhardus Vos, Louis Berkhof, Anthony Hoekema, y William Hendriksen, el último de los cuales expuso en detalle la lectura de recapitulación de Apocalipsis. Así el amilenialismo no es una novedad reciente sino la antigua y ampliamente sostenida lectura de la iglesia, defendida por muchos de sus más respetados maestros a lo largo de los siglos.

blocks.en: Objections Raised by Others
blocks.es_reference: Objeciones Planteadas por Otros

blocks.en: Those who hold the other views raise serious objections, and fairness requires that they be given their full weight. The chief objection concerns the first resurrection. In Revelation 20 the same word is used for those who "lived and reigned with Christ" and for "the rest of the dead" who "did not live again until the thousand years were finished"; and since the second plainly means a bodily resurrection, critics argue that the first should mean a bodily resurrection too, so that taking one as spiritual and the other as bodily is inconsistent. Second, they argue that reading chapters nineteen and twenty in sequence is the natural reading, and that recapitulation, however common elsewhere, must here be assumed rather than proved. Third, they observe that Satan appears very active and powerful in the present age, prowling like a roaring lion and blinding the minds of unbelievers, which seems hard to square with his being bound. Fourth, they question the figurative reading of the thousand years and ask why the passage should not be taken literally. Some add that amillennialism does not do full justice to the Old Testament promises of an earthly kingdom or to the future of Israel. Amillennialists reply that the first resurrection is paired with the second death and so belongs to the spiritual order, that recapitulation is a genuine feature of the book, and that Satan's binding is limited to the deceiving of the nations.
blocks.es_reference: Los que sostienen las otras vistas plantean objeciones serias, y la justicia exige que se les dé todo su peso. La principal objeción se refiere a la primera resurrección. En Apocalipsis 20 se usa la misma palabra para los que "vivieron y reinaron con Cristo" y para "los otros muertos" que "no volvieron a vivir hasta que se cumplieron mil años"; y puesto que el segundo claramente significa una resurrección corporal, los críticos argumentan que el primero debería significar una resurrección corporal también, de modo que tomar uno como espiritual y el otro como corporal es inconsistente. Segundo, argumentan que leer los capítulos diecinueve y veinte en secuencia es la lectura natural, y que la recapitulación, por común que sea en otros lugares, aquí debe suponerse más que probarse. Tercero, observan que Satanás aparece muy activo y poderoso en la presente edad, rondando como león rugiente y cegando las mentes de los incrédulos, lo cual parece difícil de armonizar con que esté atado. Cuarto, cuestionan la lectura figurada de los mil años y preguntan por qué el pasaje no debería tomarse literalmente. Algunos añaden que el amilenialismo no hace plena justicia a las promesas del Antiguo Testamento de un reino terrenal ni al futuro de Israel. Los amilenialistas responden que la primera resurrección está emparejada con la muerte segunda y por tanto pertenece al orden espiritual, que la recapitulación es un rasgo genuino del libro, y que el atar de Satanás se limita al engaño de las naciones.

blocks.en: Summary and an Even-Handed Word
blocks.es_reference: Resumen y una Palabra Imparcial

blocks.en: The strength claimed for amillennialism is that it fits the pattern of the rest of the New Testament, which sets the resurrection, the judgment, and the new creation at one coming; that it takes seriously the symbolism and the recapitulating structure of Revelation; and that it has been the church's majority reading for most of its history. Its central claim is that the thousand years are the present age, that Christ reigns now, and that there is no earthly millennium before or after His single return. Sincere, godly, orthodox Christians have held this view, among them many of the church's greatest theologians, and the course presents it at full strength without endorsing it, just as it has presented the other two. This completes the three views. Postmillennialism looks for a golden age of gospel triumph before Christ returns; premillennialism looks for a literal earthly reign after He returns; amillennialism understands the thousand years as the present age, with Christ reigning now. The course favors none of the three and urges students to study the Scriptures and weigh the views before God. What all three confess together, and what matters above every difference, is that the Lord Jesus Christ will surely return in glory, raise the dead, judge the world in righteousness, and reign forever with His people in the new creation.
blocks.es_reference: La fortaleza que se reclama para el amilenialismo es que encaja con el patrón del resto del Nuevo Testamento, que pone la resurrección, el juicio, y la nueva creación en una sola venida; que toma en serio el simbolismo y la estructura recapituladora de Apocalipsis; y que ha sido la lectura mayoritaria de la iglesia durante la mayor parte de su historia. Su afirmación central es que los mil años son la presente edad, que Cristo reina ahora, y que no hay milenio terrenal antes ni después de su única venida. Cristianos sinceros, piadosos, y ortodoxos han sostenido esta vista, entre ellos muchos de los más grandes teólogos de la iglesia, y el curso la presenta a plena fuerza sin respaldarla, tal como ha presentado las otras dos. Esto completa las tres vistas. El postmilenialismo busca una edad de oro de triunfo del evangelio antes de que Cristo regrese; el premilenialismo busca un reinado terrenal literal después de que regrese; el amilenialismo entiende los mil años como la presente edad, con Cristo reinando ahora. El curso no favorece ninguna de las tres y exhorta a los estudiantes a estudiar las Escrituras y sopesar las vistas delante de Dios. Lo que las tres confiesan juntas, y lo que importa sobre toda diferencia, es que el Señor Jesucristo ciertamente regresará en gloria, resucitará a los muertos, juzgará al mundo en justicia, y reinará para siempre con su pueblo en la nueva creación.

mc.stem: The prefix "a" in "amillennialism" signals that this view expects:
options: No literal, earthly thousand-year reign after Christ's return
mc.why: "A" means "no": no literal earthly millennium follows Christ's return.

mc.stem: Amillennialism teaches that the thousand years of Revelation 20 symbolize:
mc.why: Amillennialism takes the thousand years as the present age between Christ's comings.

mc.stem: In amillennialism, Christ reigns:
options: Now, from heaven, during the present age
Not at all until His return
mc.why: Amillennialism holds that Christ reigns now from heaven over His kingdom.

mc.stem: In amillennialism, the binding of Satan means:
options: He is restrained from deceiving the nations so as to stop the gospel
mc.why: Satan is bound for a purpose: he cannot deceive the nations to halt the gospel.

mc.stem: Amillennialism understands the "first resurrection" (20:4-6) as:
options: A spiritual rising — regeneration, or the soul living and reigning with Christ
mc.why: Amillennialists read the first resurrection spiritually, not as a bodily rising.

mc.stem: In amillennialism, how many bodily resurrections and final judgments are there?
options: Two of each, a thousand years apart
One of each, at Christ's single return
mc.why: One general resurrection and one judgment occur at Christ's single coming.

mc.stem: Amillennialism expects, before the end:
options: No earthly golden age; the wheat and tares grow together as both good and evil ripen
mc.why: Amillennialism expects good and evil to grow together until the harvest (Matt 13).

mc.stem: Amillennialism reads Revelation 20 in relation to chapter 19 as:
options: Recapitulation — chapter 20 retells the present age from a new angle, not a period after chapter 19
mc.why: Amillennialism reads ch. 20 as recapitulating the age, not following ch. 19 in time.

mc.stem: For the spiritual sense of the first resurrection, amillennialists appeal to texts such as:
options: John 5:24-25 and Ephesians 2, on being raised with Christ now
mc.why: They cite John 5:24-25 and Ephesians 2:1-6 for the believer's present spiritual life.

mc.stem: For the binding of Satan, amillennialists appeal to Christ's first-coming victory in texts such as:
mc.why: They cite the binding of the strong man and Satan's fall at Christ's first coming.

mc.stem: Amillennialists stress that the rest of the New Testament presents Christ's return as bringing:
options: Resurrection, judgment, and the new creation together at one coming
mc.why: They argue the NT sets resurrection, judgment, and new creation at one coming.

mc.stem: The decisive figure who shaped amillennialism and turned the church from chiliasm was:
mc.why: Augustine's City of God set out the amillennial reading that came to dominate.

mc.stem: Amillennialism became the dominant view of:
options: The medieval church, and remains common in Catholic, Lutheran, and Reformed theology
mc.why: It dominated the medieval church and remains common in those traditions today.

mc.stem: Modern proponents of amillennialism include:
mc.why: Berkhof, Hoekema, Vos, and Hendriksen are notable modern amillennialists.

mc.stem: A strength claimed for amillennialism is that it fits:
options: The single-coming pattern and takes Revelation's symbolism and recapitulation seriously
mc.why: Amillennialists claim it fits the NT single-coming pattern and Revelation's symbolism.

mc.stem: A leading objection others raise is that the "first resurrection" reads more naturally as:
options: Bodily — since the same word "lived" is used for it and for the resurrection of the rest of the dead
mc.why: Critics argue the parallel wording makes both resurrections bodily.

mc.stem: Critics also argue that reading Revelation 19-20 in sequence, rather than as recapitulation, is:
mc.why: Critics say the sequential reading is natural and recapitulation must be assumed.

mc.stem: Another objection is that Satan, in the present age, seems:
options: Very active and powerful — prowling like a roaring lion
mc.why: Critics cite 1 Peter 5:8 to question how Satan can be said to be bound.

mc.stem: Critics further question amillennialism's:
options: Figurative reading of the thousand years and its handling of Old Testament earthly-kingdom promises
mc.why: Critics question the figurative reading and the handling of OT kingdom promises.

mc.stem: The course presents amillennialism:
options: At full strength, without endorsing it, since godly Christians hold it
mc.why: The course favors no view and presents each fairly and at full strength.

sa.prompt: What does amillennialism hold about the millennium and the reign of Christ?
sa.model: The prefix a means no, and so the name signals that amillennialism expects no literal, earthly thousand-year reign of Christ following His return. Instead, amillennialism teaches that the thousand years of Revelation 20 are a symbol of the entire present age, the whole span between the first and second comings of Christ. During this age Christ reigns now from heaven over His kingdom, the souls of the faithful who have died live and reign with Him, and Satan is restrained from deceiving the nations so as to stop the spread of the gospel. There is no separate earthly kingdom between Christ's return and the eternal state. When Christ comes again, there is one general resurrection of the righteous and the wicked, one final judgment, and then immediately the new heaven and the new earth. Amillennialism therefore reads Revelation 20 as describing the church age in which believers now live, rather than a future period on earth, and it understands the millennium as a present spiritual reality rather than a coming political one.

sa.prompt: Describe the amillennial order of events.
sa.model: The amillennial order is the simplest of the three. The present church age is itself the millennium, the time in which Christ reigns from heaven, the gospel goes to the nations, and the departed saints reign with Christ. Throughout this age, amillennialists hold, the kingdom grows and the gospel spreads, but evil also continues and even intensifies, for the wheat and the tares grow together until the harvest, and both ripen toward the end. There is no earthly golden age to be expected before the return, nor an earthly reign to follow it. At the close of the age Satan is loosed for a little while in a final assault, which is the brief loosing of Revelation 20. Then Christ returns, once and visibly. At His single coming the dead are raised, the righteous and the wicked together, in one general resurrection; all stand before the great white throne for one final judgment; and then God brings in the new heaven and the new earth at once. So the whole drama turns on one return, one resurrection, and one judgment, without any thousand-year reign on the earth before or after.

sa.prompt: Summarize the biblical case amillennialists make.
sa.model: Amillennialists build their case from the wider New Testament as well as from Revelation. They argue that the first resurrection of Revelation 20 is a spiritual rather than a bodily rising. Some take it as the new birth, since Scripture speaks of believers as already raised with Christ and made alive together with Him while they live on earth; others take it as the entrance of the believer's soul into life and reign with Christ at death. They appeal for the binding of Satan to the victory of Christ's first coming, when the strong man was bound, Satan fell like lightning, and the ruler of this world was cast out, so that the nations he once held in darkness now hear the gospel. They stress that the rest of the New Testament presents the second coming as a single event bringing the resurrection of all, the final judgment, and the new creation together, not in stages separated by a thousand years. And they point to the many texts that show Christ already enthroned and reigning now, until He has put all His enemies under His feet.

sa.prompt: How does amillennialism read Revelation 20, including recapitulation, the thousand years, the binding, and the first resurrection?
sa.model: The key to the amillennial reading is that Revelation often circles back over the same ground, showing the same period again and again from new angles, as it does with the seals, the trumpets, and the bowls. On this principle, called recapitulation, chapter twenty does not follow chapter nineteen in time but returns to the beginning of the present age and views it afresh. The thousand years are taken as a symbolic number, signifying a long and complete period rather than a literal span of exactly one thousand calendar years. The binding of Satan is his restraint, by the power of Christ's first coming, from deceiving the nations so as to prevent the gospel from going out to them; he is bound for that purpose, though still active in other ways. The first resurrection is the spiritual life and reign of believers, whether in regeneration or in the life of the soul with Christ after death. At the end of the age Satan is loosed briefly, and then come the return of Christ and the one judgment of the closing verses. So Revelation 20, read this way, pictures the present age and not a future earthly kingdom.

sa.prompt: Who shaped amillennialism, and what is its history?
sa.model: Amillennialism has the longest record as the majority view of the church through most of its history. The decisive figure was Augustine, whose work The City of God set out the reading that the thousand years are the present age and that the reign of the saints is spiritual. Under his influence the church largely turned away from the earlier expectation of an earthly reign, and amillennialism became the dominant view of the medieval church for a thousand years. The Reformers, including Luther and Calvin, stood broadly in this tradition, though the technical terms came later. The view remains common in Roman Catholic, Lutheran, and much of Reformed theology to this day. In modern times it has been carefully expounded by scholars such as Geerhardus Vos, Louis Berkhof, Anthony Hoekema, and William Hendriksen, the last of whom set out the recapitulation reading of Revelation in detail. So amillennialism is not a recent novelty but the ancient and widely held reading of the church, defended by many of its most respected teachers across the centuries.

sa.prompt: How does amillennialism understand the binding of Satan and the present reign of Christ?
sa.model: Amillennialism understands the binding of Satan as a real but limited restraint rather than total inactivity. By the power of Christ's first coming, when the strong man was bound and the ruler of this world was cast out, Satan is restrained from deceiving the nations so as to keep the gospel from going out to them; before Christ, the nations sat in darkness, but now the gospel reaches every people. Satan remains active in other ways, tempting, accusing, and opposing, but he can no longer hold the nations as he once did or gather them to destroy the church before the appointed end. Alongside this, amillennialism stresses that Christ is already enthroned and reigning now. He rose, ascended, and sat down at the right hand of God, and the New Testament declares that He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet. So the reign of the thousand years is the present reign of Christ from heaven, in which the departed saints share, and the binding of Satan is the curbing of his power over the nations during this gospel age, not his removal from the world.

sa.prompt: What objections do others raise against amillennialism?
sa.model: Those who hold the other views raise serious objections, and fairness requires that they be given their full weight. The chief objection concerns the first resurrection. In Revelation 20 the same word is used for those who lived and reigned with Christ and for the rest of the dead who did not live again until the thousand years were finished; and since the second plainly means a bodily resurrection, critics argue that the first should mean a bodily resurrection too, so that taking one as spiritual and the other as bodily is inconsistent. Second, they argue that reading chapters nineteen and twenty in sequence is the natural reading, and that recapitulation, however common elsewhere, must here be assumed rather than proved. Third, they observe that Satan appears very active and powerful in the present age, prowling like a roaring lion and blinding the minds of unbelievers, which seems hard to square with his being bound. Fourth, they question the figurative reading of the thousand years and ask why the passage should not be taken literally. Some add that amillennialism does not do full justice to the Old Testament promises of an earthly kingdom or to the future of Israel.

sa.prompt: How do amillennialists respond to those objections?
sa.model: Amillennialists offer several replies. To the chief objection they answer that the first resurrection is set in deliberate contrast with the second death, and that this pairing places it in the spiritual and eternal order rather than the merely physical; just as the second death is not the death of the body but eternal separation from God, so the first resurrection is not the raising of the body but the believer's spiritual life and reign with Christ. They argue that the word for lived can carry different senses according to context, and that the souls who lived and reigned describe the intermediate state. They defend recapitulation as a genuine feature of Revelation, pointing to the way the seals, trumpets, and bowls cover overlapping ground, so that it is not arbitrary to read chapter twenty as returning to the start of the age. They insist that the binding of Satan is limited to the deceiving of the nations, which fits his present restraint even while he remains active in other ways. And they hold that the single-coming pattern of the rest of the New Testament should guide the reading of one symbolic passage, rather than the reverse.

sa.prompt: What is the strength of amillennialism, and what do all three millennial views share?
sa.model: The strength claimed for amillennialism is that it fits the pattern of the rest of the New Testament, which sets the resurrection, the judgment, and the new creation at one coming; that it takes seriously the symbolism and the recapitulating structure of Revelation; and that it has been the church's majority reading for most of its history. Its central claim is that the thousand years are the present age, that Christ reigns now, and that there is no earthly millennium before or after His single return. Sincere, godly, orthodox Christians have held this view, among them many of the church's greatest theologians, and the course presents it at full strength without endorsing it, just as it has presented the other two; it favors no single view. What all three views confess together, and what matters above every difference, is that the Lord Jesus Christ will surely return in glory, raise the dead, judge the world in righteousness, and reign forever with His people in the new creation. On that great hope the whole church stands together, however its members may understand the thousand years.

sa.prompt: Summarize the central claim of amillennialism even-handedly, and recap the three views.
sa.model: The central claim of amillennialism is that the thousand years of Revelation 20 are the present age, that Christ reigns now from heaven, that Satan is restrained from deceiving the nations, and that there is no earthly millennium before or after Christ's single return, which brings one resurrection, one judgment, and the new creation together. It reads Revelation 20 as recapitulation and the first resurrection as spiritual, and it has been the church's majority view since Augustine. This completes the three views. Postmillennialism looks for a golden age of gospel triumph before Christ returns; premillennialism looks for a literal earthly reign after He returns; amillennialism understands the thousand years as the present age, with Christ reigning now. Each is held by sincere, godly, orthodox Christians, each faces honest objections, and the course favors none of the three, urging students to search the Scriptures and weigh the views before God. What all three confess together, and what matters most, is that the Lord Jesus Christ will surely return in glory, raise the dead, judge the world, and reign forever with His people.
